title: Late Breaking Results: On-the-Fly Hadamard Hypervector Processing for Efficient Hyperdimensional Computing
problem: Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) requires expensive pre-generation or iterative O(N) search to find orthogonal hypervectors, creating bottleneck for hardware deployment; fixed precomputed vectors limit adaptability.
method: Introduces on-the-fly hypervector generation in hardware using Hadamard binary coefficients with O(1) complexity versus O(N) conventional search. Leverages unary computing and in-memory computing (IMC) to simplify encoding into addition-only operations after generation. ASIC implementation leverages Hadamard properties for efficient hardware realization.

title: Process-Variation-Aware Design Optimization for Wavelength-Routed Optical Networks-on-Chip
problem: Wavelength-routed optical NoCs use microring resonators (MRRs) for collision-free communication, but manufacturing process variation shifts MRR transmission spectra, reducing signal power and increasing crosstalk.
method: Methodology constructs analytical models of expected signal transmission power under MRR process variation. Optimization jointly tunes MRR radii and signal wavelengths to maximize expected signal power despite process variation. Joint tuning exploits coupled effects between geometry and wavelength selection.

title: FHENDI: A Near-DRAM Accelerator for Compiler-Generated Fully Homomorphic Encryption Applications
problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) workloads are both compute- and memory-intensive, and even dedicated FHE ASICs are bottlenecked by expensive memory transfers due to large ciphertext operands and limited bank-to-bank communication, die-to-die bandwidth, and memory access latency within near-DRAM processing.
method: FHENDI is a hierarchical near-DRAM processing (NDP) architecture that exploits four levels of FHE parallelism (element-wise, limb-wise, coefficient-wise, ciphertext-wise) mapped to different hierarchy levels. Bank-to-bank communication is addressed via a conflict-free mapping algorithm using localized permutation networks that enable element-wise and butterfly operations within DRAM subarrays. Die-to-die bandwidth constraints are addressed by pipelining parallel bootstrapping operations identified by the HElayers compiler. Memory access latency is hidden using a dual-banking scheme combined with subarray-level parallelism (SLP). The system is evaluated with compiled FHE programs for CNN/Transformer ML inference, database range query, and sorting.

title: CXLfork: Fast Remote Fork over CXL Fabrics
problem: Remote process cloning across cluster nodes incurs high serialization and copying overhead, creating large cold-start latency for serverless functions and other scale-out workloads. Traditional fork() semantics do not map efficiently to distributed shared memory environments like CXL-attached memory.
method: CXLfork implements a remote fork interface that uses CXL-attached shared memory to achieve near-zero-serialization, zero-copy process cloning across nodes. It stores process state (pages, metadata) in globally-shared CXL memory for cluster-wide deduplication, so cloning a process on a remote node avoids transferring state over the network. Fine-grained tiering between local DRAM and CXL memory is supported, allowing hot pages to remain local while cold/shared pages reside in CXL memory. CXL-porter builds on top of CXLfork as an efficient horizontal autoscaler for serverless functions.

title: High Density Si-IPD Technologies as Enabler for High-Performance and Low-Power Consumption Processor Chips
problem: Power delivery networks in high-performance processors require large on-chip capacitance with minimal area footprint; traditional discrete capacitors consume significant board space. Si-IPD (Silicon Integrated Passive Devices) with high-density silicon capacitors integrate voltage regulation directly on-chip.
method: High-density Si-IPD technology integrates silicon capacitors and inductors directly into processor chips using specialized fabrication techniques, achieving higher capacitance density than traditional approaches and reducing parasitic resistance and inductance in the power delivery path.

title: Bit-Separable Transformer Accelerator Leveraging Output Activation Sparsity for Efficient DRAM Access
problem: Transformer inference is memory-bound; DRAM bandwidth limits throughput, especially for attention operations where memory access patterns are irregular.
method: The accelerator uses bit-separable representation for sparse activations, compressing output activations to reduce DRAM traffic. It combines this with specialized access patterns optimizing for sparse memory reads/writes.

title: EDGE: DBMS-Empowered Boolean Decomposition for GIG Synthesis
problem: Boolean decomposition-based logic synthesis is high-quality but computationally expensive, limiting application to large and complex logic functions in modern circuit design.
method: EDGE leverages modern database (DBMS) techniques to accelerate Boolean decomposition queries and candidate enumeration. Database queries replace iterative decomposition searches, exploiting relational query optimization to speedup candidate generation and evaluation for Gate-Inverter Graph synthesis.

title: Centralized Training and Decentralized Control through the Actor-Critic Paradigm for Highly Optimized Multicores
problem: Distributed neural-network-based resource controllers suffer from conflicting control decisions and partial observability, significantly impairing learning and stability of control policies for multicore systems.
method: A centralized neural-network critic evaluates global system behavior under temperature constraints while decentralized neural-network actors implement core-level DVFS decisions trained together via actor-critic reinforcement learning, resolving conflicting decisions and improving observability.

title: DSPlacer: DSP Placement for FPGA-based CNN Accelerator
problem: FPGA-based CNN accelerator placement suffers from timing closure challenges; DSP placement directly impacts clock frequency and throughput but lacks automated optimization.
method: DSPlacer optimizes datapath DSP placement iteratively using graph convolutional network-based identification, DSP graph construction, min-cost-flow assignment, and integer linear programming (ILP) for cascade constraint legalization.

title: 21.7 Merging Hybrid and Multi-Phase Topologies: A 6-Phase Triple-Step-Down DC-DC Converter Achieving up to a 60:1 Voltage Conversion Ratio and 868A/cm3 Current Density
problem: Modern processors require efficient point-of-load DC-DC converters delivering high current (>1A) at extreme voltage step-down (12V to <1V); conventional single-phase buck struggles with large step-down/current, hybrid converters scale poorly with current (flying capacitors), and multi-phase designs require more inductor inductance.
method: A 6-phase triple-step-down hybrid-multi-phase architecture combines the inductance advantages of multi-phase designs with flying-capacitor efficiency of hybrid topologies. Instead of scaling flying capacitors, the design exploits multiple compact inductors, achieving lower total volume and higher current density with reduced DCR.

title: iTaskSense: Task-Oriented Object Detection in Resource-Constrained Environments
problem: Efficient task-oriented object detection on edge/resource-constrained devices; conventional models require extensive datasets and struggle with generalization to diverse real-world scenarios.
method: iTask framework leverages LLMs to generalize from limited samples via abstract knowledge graph encoding task attributes. Two configuration models: (1) distilled task-specific vision transformer for defined tasks (15% higher accuracy); (2) quantized model for multi-task robustness. Custom hardware acceleration circuit supports real-time edge processing.

title: 29.5 A 3nm 3.6GHz Dual-Port SRAM with Backend-RC Optimization and a Far-End Write-Assist Scheme
problem: Dual-port SRAM design at 3nm process nodes suffers from increased resistance-capacitance (RC) degradation, complex timing constraints from asynchronous dual-clock operation, and challenges maintaining write margins across wide voltage/temperature ranges.
method: The design combines array dual-rail (ADR) voltage management with VDI for periphery and VDDM for cell arrays, introduces a far-end write-assist scheme to strengthen write margins, and updates wakeup circuitry to handle complex voltage relationships (VDD > VDDM > VSS constraints).

title: ANVIL: An In-Storage Accelerator for Name-Value Data Stores
problem: Large-scale name-value pair (NVP) lookups saturate both external and internal SSD bandwidth because every NVP must be sent to the host CPU to check for a name match. Existing NVP optimizations are limited to a single data store format, leaving the broad heterogeneity of NVP encodings unaddressed.
method: ANVIL implements in-storage processing by pushing name-match logic directly into the NAND flash chips of a conventional SSD. Rather than streaming all key-value data to the host, ANVIL performs name-match filtering inside the storage device, discarding non-matching NVPs before they traverse the SSD-host interface. The system is designed as an end-to-end in-storage accelerator that supports multiple NVP formats (arrays, dictionaries, key-value stores, data mining structures) through a unified near-storage computation model.

title: Hardware Sentinel: Protecting Software Applications from Hardware Silent Data Corruptions
problem: Silent Data Corruptions (SDCs) caused by silicon defects in CPUs propagate undetected through large-scale data center applications, causing unpredictable failures (segfaults, crashes, log anomalies) that are difficult to attribute to hardware without systematic cross-layer analysis.
method: Hardware Sentinel is a top-down framework that correlates software-layer failure indicators—segmentation faults, core dumps, application crashes, and structured logs—with underlying hardware-layer defect signals across CPUs. It builds statistical models linking application failure patterns to CPU hardware identities, enabling SDC attribution across diverse workload, kernel, and hardware configurations. The framework was validated over 6 years of failure data spanning 13 workloads across 27 data center regions, using fleet-wide telemetry ingestion and cross-referencing with out-of-production (Fleetscanner) and in-production (Ripple) hardware tests.

title: 34.4 A 9.05-to-37.0GHz LO Generator with Magnetic Mode Switching and Tuning-Free Octave-Bandwidth Common-Mode Resonator Achieving >190.7dBc/Hz FoM
problem: VCOs with octave-plus tuning range (>10GHz center frequency) face challenges maintaining low phase noise while spanning wide frequency coverage; multi-core multi-mode architectures are complex and require extensive tuning.
method: An octave-bandwidth VCO uses magnetic mode switching to transition between operating bands and implements a tuning-free common-mode resonator with automatic frequency tracking across the full tuning range, eliminating manual mode transitions.

title: Graph-Guided Transfer Learning to Boost the Efficiency of System-Level Optimization of Analog/Mixed-Signal Circuits
problem: System-level optimization of analog/mixed-signal circuits requires expensive iterative circuit simulations; transfer learning has limited applicability across dissimilar architectures.
method: Combines reinforcement learning with graph attention networks (GAT) and a graph similarity detection method to identify electrical trade-offs; transfers learned policies across different circuit topologies by recognizing structural similarities.
